title: Long-tail multi-variant load emulator for dedicated capacity regression detection
creator: Ariana Chen
description: Create a flexible load-emulation harness that can run long-duration steady-state traffic and controlled burst profiles against Dedicated pools to validate autoscaler behavior and detect regressions in tail latency (p95/p99) and tokens/sec. The emulator must simulate multiple client patterns (chat-style incremental tokens, large single-shot generations, and mixed KV-cache warm/cold scenarios), support running model variants (fp16, int8-quantized, and memory-optimized kernels), and produce regression signals tied to historical baselines. This ticket covers the harness design, implementation, dashboards, and a first full-week soak run against a staging Dedicated pool with induced fallback events to validate graceful degradation and rollout policies.
tasks: Design run matrix: steady-state QPS targets (low/med/high) + burst events (5x, 10x, 20x) + KV cache hit-rate scenarios
Implement emulator runner with token-level pacing and per-session KV cache state to model realistic chat workloads
Add model-variant hooks so same workload can test fp16 vs int8 vs memory-optimized kernels
Emit standardized metrics: tokens/sec, inferences/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, error_rate, gpu_util_pct, instance_churn, queue_length
Integrate regression detector that compares live p95 and tokens/sec to rolling baseline and raises alerts if deviation > configured thresholds
Create Grafana dashboard and alert rules; wire alerts to #dedicated-soak Slack channel and PagerDuty test escalation
Run 7-day soak against staging Dedicated pool, capture traces, and produce final report with anomaly timeline and recommended guardrails
acceptance_criteria: Harness can execute both steady-state and burst scenarios from CLI with a single run config file
Metrics collected to our metrics cluster and visible in dashboard with correct labels for model_variant and cache_hit_rate
Regression detector flags at least one synthetic regression during induced config change (quantization toggle) in test run
Autoscaler reactions (scale up/down) are observed and correlated with traffic; no service-level outage during burst injection
Final report includes comparison vs baseline and a PRD for follow-up mitigations (batching, cache heat-up, fallback routing)
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Initial design doc draft posted to Confluence (see links). Identified need to model client think-time variance to reproduce p95 drift observed in prod.
2026-03-01: Basic emulator PoC implemented. Can generate token-paced chat sessions and toggle cache hit probability. Early runs show stable tokens/sec but p95 increases with cold-cache runs.
2026-03-07: Hooked model-variant switch; tested int8 path — latency tail widened by ~12% in cold-cache synthetic runs. Added experiment flag to force quantize fallback.
2026-03-12: Dashboard prototype up; regression-detector logic implemented using moving window z-score on p95 and tokens/sec. Began configuring alert thresholds for staging soak.
2026-03-14: Kicking off first 7-day soak on staging Dedicated pool with scheduled induced fallback at 36h. Assigned follow-ups for tighter autoscaler cool-down window if oscillation observed.
